questions.question: The minimum sea surface temperature needed for tropical cyclone formation is about:
options: Twenty-six and a half to twenty-seven degrees Celsius, warm to roughly fifty metres deep
Twenty degrees Celsius at the surface only
Thirty-five degrees Celsius
Any temperature, as long as the water is deep

questions.question: No tropical cyclone is ever born on the equator because:
options: The water there is too cold
The Coriolis force is zero there, so converging air cannot be set spinning
The trade winds are too strong there
There is no ocean on the equator

questions.question: Strong wind shear prevents cyclone growth by:
options: Cooling the ocean surface
Adding too much moisture
Slicing the tops off the rising thunderstorm towers and scattering the released heat
Reversing the Coriolis force

questions.question: The storms that threaten southern Africa are born:
options: In the North Atlantic, where they are called hurricanes
Off the Cape coast in winter
In the Benguela current
In the south-west Indian Ocean east of Madagascar, from November to April

subtopics.title: Stages of Growth and the Anatomy of the Storm

questions.question: A system is first given a name when it reaches the stage of:
options: Tropical disturbance
Tropical depression
Tropical storm, with winds between 63 and 118 km/h
Category five

questions.question: The eye of a mature cyclone is calm and clear because:
options: Air there is sinking, warming and drying, which dissolves cloud
The wind blows straight up through it
It lies outside the storm
Cold air pools there

questions.question: The most violent winds and heaviest rain are found in the:
options: Outer rain bands
Eye wall — the ring of tallest cumulonimbus around the eye
Eye itself
Trailing cold front

questions.question: The cyclone strengthens in a self-feeding loop because condensation in the eye wall:
options: Cools the storm's core
Blocks the inflowing air
Raises the central pressure
Releases latent heat, deepening the low and pulling the inward spiral harder

subtopics.title: The Weather Sequence and Why the Storm Dies

questions.question: The first sign of an approaching cyclone, often a day or more ahead, is:
options: Long ocean swells arriving on a still-calm shore, with high thin cloud thickening
The eye passing overhead
A sudden temperature drop
Snow on the coast

questions.question: Historically, the greatest killer in tropical cyclones has been:
options: Lightning strikes
Hail damage
The storm surge — a wind-driven dome of sea pushed over low coasts
The calm of the eye

questions.question: Leaving shelter when the eye arrives is deadly because:
options: The eye lasts for several days
The far eye wall arrives within the hour, with the wind reversed in direction
The air in the eye is poisonous
The pressure in the eye is dangerously high

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the three ways a tropical cyclone dies?
options: Making landfall and losing its evaporation supply
Moving over cool water poleward of thirty degrees
Being torn apart by strong upper wind shear
Crossing the equator into the other hemisphere

subtopics.title: Case Study, Satellite Identification and Management

questions.question: Cyclone Idai intensified into a full cyclone because it:
options: Crossed the cold Benguela current
Merged with a cold front
Stayed over the Kalahari
Drifted back over the warm Mozambique Channel and refuelled before striking Beira

questions.question: The deadly mudslides of Idai struck around Chimanimani in Zimbabwe partly because:
options: Deforested slopes gave way under extreme rainfall
The storm surge reached the mountains
An earthquake struck at the same time
The area lies below sea level

questions.question: On satellite imagery, the one-look difference between the two cyclone families is:
options: Colour of the cloud tops
Tropical: tight circle with an eye in low latitudes; mid-latitude: open comma with trailing fronts further poleward
Tropical systems have no cloud
Mid-latitude systems are always smaller

questions.question: Which is a BEFORE-the-storm management strategy?
options: Restoring power lines
Distributing cholera medication in flooded settlements
Conserving mangrove belts as natural surge barriers and rehearsing evacuation routes
Waiting for the eye to pass

subtopics.title: The Pot, the Spin and the Birth Rules

questions.question: In the boiling-pot picture, the cyclone's fuel is:
options: Latent heat, repaid when water vapour condenses back into cloud droplets
The heat of the sand on the beach
Electricity from lightning
The cold air above the storm

questions.question: The spinning skater explains that the storm gains its rotation because:
options: The ocean currents spin it
The moon pulls it around
Thunderstorms naturally rotate
Inward-rushing air is curved by the Coriolis effect and speeds up as it draws in, like a skater pulling in her arms

questions.question: The equator is a closed dance floor for cyclones because:
options: The water there is too rough
The Coriolis effect is zero on the equator, so nothing can be set spinning there
The trade winds blow the storms away
There is too much rain there already

subtopics.title: The Doughnut With the Hole in the Middle

questions.question: In the doughnut picture, the hole, the ring and the arms are:
options: The surge, the swell and the tide
Three different storms
The eye, the eye wall and the spiral rain bands
The three stages of growth

questions.question: A town under the passing rain bands experiences:
options: Rain in pulses — squall, breather, harder squall — heavier as the centre nears
One continuous unchanging downpour
Complete calm throughout
Snow flurries

questions.question: The golden rule about the sudden stillness mid-storm is:
options: It means the storm is over and it is safe outside
It is the eye — stay sheltered, because the far wall arrives within the hour with the wind reversed
It only happens at night
It signals the arrival of a cold front

questions.question: The straw picture of the storm surge shows that:
options: The surge is caused by heavy rain filling the sea
The surge only happens at low tide
The wind alone lifts the sea
Extreme low pressure lifts the sea surface like liquid up a straw, and the wind then drives that raised water ashore

subtopics.title: Idai, the Fuel Gauge and Being Ready

questions.question: Idai is the perfect fuel-gauge story because it:
options: Weakened over land, refuelled over the warm Mozambique Channel, and returned to strike Beira as a full cyclone
Never touched land at all
Formed over the Kalahari
Was stopped by the escarpment

questions.question: After the wind died, the killer that stalked Idai's flooded settlements was:
options: Frostbite
Cholera, spread through contaminated water
Heatstroke
Lightning

questions.question: From space, the tropical cyclone and the mid-latitude cyclone are told apart as:
options: Two identical commas
A square versus a triangle
A pinwheel with a dark dot versus an open comma with a long tail
A white disc versus a black disc

questions.question: The sentence that completes a management answer is:
options: Storms are impossible to predict, so nothing can be done
Only the wind speed determines the damage
Evacuation should happen after the storm
The hazard is natural, but the size of the disaster is partly human — settlement, deforestation and warnings decide the toll
